herramientas.descripcion:
Moves a decision from 'proposed' to 'accepted'. It is the ONLY way to accept a decision and the client asks
for the user's approval on every call. `user_quote`: the user's literal words confirming it in the chat (stored
in the ADR as evidence). Never call it without that confirmation.

Accepts SEVERAL proposals with a single user approval; the user sees the full list when approving. Use it only
when the user explicitly accepted those decisions in the same message; `user_quote` is that literal message.
All or nothing: if any of them is not proposed or does not exist, none is accepted.

Records an open question or unresolved topic. Idempotent (ADR-019): if a pending item with this topic
(ignoring case and spaces) was created in the last minutes AND is STILL 'open', nothing new is created and the
existing id is returned. If that item was already closed, a human already intervened, so a new one is recorded.

Extends a task that has not run yet (status todo) or was sent back (changes_requested) with additional
acceptance criteria and/or notes. Any other status is rejected (after a review, use request_changes).
Appends a dated "### Amendment N" block (sub-labels "Additional criteria" / "Notes") to the task's "Amendments"
section; the original criteria stay untouched. One commit per amendment; give at least one of the three fields.
`delegation`: sets the task's exception to the delegation policy (ADR-036), "required" or "off", in its
frontmatter (empty = unchanged); it adds no Amendment block by itself.
Idempotent (ADR-019): an identical amendment recorded in the last minutes is not written again.
Closes a pending item (status 'closed'). If the resolution produced a decision, give its decision_id.

Creates a NEW text file in an allowed area (by default .project/ and docs/). Fails if it already exists.
Separate from update_document so the user can require approval for creating files.

Creates a work specification for the coding agent in .project/tasks/T-NNN.md (status 'todo').
In multi-repo projects, `repo` (required) is the folder where the work happens; in single-repo projects it is
ignored (the response says so).
It must be self-contained: the coding agent runs it without this chat. `acceptance_criteria`: a verifiable list
(tests that must pass, observable behavior). `decisions`: applicable ADR ids. `files`: paths likely to be
touched. The user runs it with /run-task T-NNN.
`resolves`: pending items the task resolves, comma-separated, each optionally with "(partial)" (e.g.
"P-036, P-037 (partial)"); they must exist and be open. Stored in the task ("Resolves" section); when the task is
merged, update_task reminds which ones are still open. It never closes pending items.
`delegation`: the task's exception to the delegation policy, decided while planning (ADR-036): "required" or
"off" (empty = inherit from the project/global policy). Use "off" when the task touches security, is
cross-cutting, or depends on diagnosing a cause the spec does not know yet. Stored in the task's frontmatter.
The response adds the line of detected integrations (not written into the task).
Idempotent (ADR-019): if a task with this title (ignoring case and spaces) was created in the last minutes AND is
STILL 'todo', nothing new is created and the existing id is returned (with the /run-task command to repeat to
the user). If that task already changed status (e.g. in_progress: it is running), a human or the coding agent
already intervened, so a new task is recorded.

ONLY for apps that support MCP forms (elicitation), such as Claude Code. In Claude Desktop or claude.ai do NOT
use it: call review_proposals and present the options (accept / adjust / reject / postpone) with your own cards
or multiple-choice questions; then apply accept_decision or reject_decision as the user chooses.
Opens one form per pending proposal; the answers come from the user without going through the model, so
acceptances and rejections are applied directly. Returns the summary and the proposals to adjust.

Start of a chat: returns INDEX.md and the open items (one line each: id, topic, date; read the detail with
read_document). Call it before answering.
The first line is `ratifact <build>` (version + content hash of the running server). Below it, a ⚠ line when
this server process is older than the installation on disk (restart the client) or when the local source it was
installed from is newer than the installation (reinstall).
At the end, if optional integrations are active (codegraph, gentle-ai, engram…), one line listing them and their
planning guidance; that guidance is conditional: follow it only if you have their tools.

Creates the empty .project/ structure of a registered project (idempotent), in the current schema (v2:
decisions/, pending/, sessions/, tasks/, content_language "en").

Lists files (with size) under a project folder.
In .project/decisions, pending and tasks it lists one record per line: "ID · status · title  (path)".
A path with a v1 folder (.project/tareas, decisiones, pendientes, sesiones) is translated and flagged.
If the full listing is too large, it is summarized by levels: unexpanded folders with their file count
("module/ (38 files)"); ask for a more specific `folder` to see the detail.
Lists the registered projects, their code folder and whether they already have a memory.

Lists the code tasks with their status and branch. Closed ones (merged, discarded) only with
include_closed=True.
End of a chat (close prompt): appends the session summary to sessions/YYYY-MM-DD.md.

Returns, ready to copy, the Claude project instructions and the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md block with the right
project name. Give them to the user as they are, without summarizing.

Creates an ADR. It is ALWAYS 'proposed'. To accept it, call accept_decision afterwards: that tool asks for
the user's approval. `summary`: one line for the decisions view.
Idempotent (ADR-019): if an ADR with this title (ignoring case and spaces) was created in the last minutes AND
is STILL 'proposed', nothing new is created and the existing id is returned. If that ADR already changed status
(e.g. rejected: the user asked for another version), a human already intervened, so a new ADR is recorded.

Reads a project text file, optionally a line range (1-based, inclusive).
Also accepts a memory record id ("T-24", "tasks/T-024.md", "ADR-020-slug.md"): if the path does not exist, it
reads the real record and prepends the line "(→ .project/<folder>/<file>)". A path with a v1 folder
(.project/tareas/…, .project/acuerdos.md…) is translated and flagged the same way.
For a task, read_task returns a working brief (spec, amendments, the latest relevant block) instead.

Working brief of a task, instead of reading the whole file: the frontmatter, the full spec (Goal, Acceptance
criteria, Resolves, Applicable decisions, Files involved, Out of scope, Notes, Amendments, How to verify), every
Amendment block, the block relevant to the status in full (changes_requested → latest Review; in_review or
failed → latest Result block; in_progress → the latest Review it answers) and a one-line index (heading · line
range · size) of every other Result/Review block, readable with read_document and that range.

Registers a project: adds it to projects.json, initializes its memory (its own git repo) and returns the
instructions to paste into Claude and into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. `path`: the code folder (must exist inside the
projects folder). `memory`: optional; by default <projects folder>/.ratifact/<name>, outside the code
repository. `tests`: command to run the tests; if omitted it is detected (Maven, Gradle, npm/pnpm/yarn, Godot,
pytest, cargo, go). Only with the user's confirmation.

Closes a proposal the user does NOT approve. It becomes 'rejected' with its reason (it is not deleted: the
history keeps what was considered and why it was not adopted). Only on the user's explicit instruction.

Sends a task in review back so the coding agent fixes it on the SAME branch.
Use it only when the user, after reviewing the result, decides to ask for changes.
`findings`: what is approved and what fails, and why. `additional_criteria`: a verifiable list of what the fix
must meet (added to the original criteria). The task becomes 'changes_requested' and is re-run with
/run-task T-NNN, which continues on the existing branch without rewriting earlier commits.
To extend a task that has not run yet (todo), use amend_task.

Returns the decisions in 'proposed' status so the user can decide to accept, adjust or reject them.
Paginated: `limit` per page (max 25) starting at `from_id` (e.g. "ADR-020"). With `summary=True` it returns one
line per proposal (useful to see the overview before going into detail).

Searches text (case-insensitive) in the project's text files and returns snippets with path and line. Use
it before reading whole documents.
Memory records come first ("ID · status · title (path)"): the one whose id is `query` (e.g. "T-1", "adr-20")
and up to 5 whose title contains it at the start of a word; then memory lines and code lines, sharing the rest
equally. In each section, files whose name contains `query` at the start of a word or camelCase part come first
(if no line matches: "path: (file name matches)"), and one line per file is shown before repeating files.
`max_results` counts every line; if something is left out, the last line says how many lines (and files) per
section.

Marks a decision as superseded by another one already recorded (status 'superseded'; decisions are never
deleted).

Modifies an EXISTING text file in an allowed area. mode: 'replace' | 'append'.
To create a new file use create_document.

Rewrites INDEX.md (the project's executive summary). It must be a regenerated SUMMARY, not an
accumulation; limit ~6000 characters.

Updates a project already registered in projects.json without editing it by hand. Give at least one of
`path`, `tests`, `repo`, `redetect=True`, `integrations`, `models` or `delegation`; with none, it returns an error and leaves the file
untouched.
`path`: new code folder, when it moved. Same checks as register_project (inside the projects folder, an
existing folder, and not containing the project's memory — ADR-010). If the project is multi-repo and the stored
`tests` keeps keys that are no longer repos under the new path, the change is applied anyway but the response
lists them and suggests `redetect=True`.
`tests`: command the coding agent uses to verify tasks (/run-task). In multi-repo projects, `repo` says which
repo it applies to.
`redetect`: True to detect the command again from the project files instead of giving it with `tests` (both at
once are incompatible). In a single-repo project it redetects the whole command; in a multi-repo one it
redetects all repos, or only `repo` if given.
`integrations`: turns optional integrations of the project on or off, e.g. "codegraph=off,gentle-ai=auto"
(values auto|off; default auto: used when detected). One turned off never appears in any response.
`models`: the project's exceptions to the global models per role (settings.json next to projects.json), e.g.
"explore=haiku,write=sonnet" (roles explore, write, verify; the value is the client's model name). "inherit"
removes the project's exception for that role, which then uses the global one (or the session's model).
`delegation`: the project's exception to the delegation policy (ADR-036): required | suggested | off; "inherit"
removes it (the global policy in settings.json applies, default required). A task can still override it.

Changes a task's status (todo, in_progress, in_review, failed, merged, discarded; the Spanish names pendiente,
en_curso, en_revision, fallida, integrada, descartada are still accepted until 1.1). Stored in English.
`result`: what was done, tests run and their summarized output, deviations from the spec.
'merged' and 'discarded' only with the user's explicit confirmation.
To ask for corrections after reviewing a task use `request_changes`, not this status change.
With 'in_progress', the response brings the guidance of active integrations (execute, verify, close), computed at
that moment; it is conditional: follow it only if you have those tools. It is not written into the task.
It also brings a "Model routing" block when the user configured models per role (explore, write, verify), and
the "Delegation" block of the effective policy (task > project > global, default required; ADR-036): with
required it is an instruction, with suggested a suggestion, with off there is none. The effective models and
policy are recorded in the task's frontmatter as `routing:` (overwritten on re-runs), together with the server
build and the time of the transition (ADR-037).
If this server process is older than the installation on disk, 'in_progress' is refused without changing
anything (restart the client and repeat it); every other status works and carries a warning.
With 'in_review', if the policy was required and `result` has no valid `Workers:` line, the response carries a
warning with a proposed corrected line when it can derive one (the status changes anyway). If the task is already
in review and `result` is only a valid `Workers:` line, it replaces that line in the latest result block instead of
adding a block (ADR-041). The routing also records the MCP client (`client=`).
With 'merged', if the task declares `resolves`, the response reminds which pending items are still open (it
never closes or modifies any).

prompts.descripcion: Closes the session: records decisions, pending items and the session log, and regenerates INDEX.md
Loads the project context before starting to work
